LESSON: HANDLING HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Foundations of Pre - Technical Studies
Topic 1.2: Handling Hazardous Substances

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Handling Hazardous Substances. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are hazardous substances labelled?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify hazardous substances found in the environment
2. classify hazardous substances found in the locality
3. describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment
4. appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HANDLING HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Handling Hazardous Substances helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: HANDLING HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES
Study Handling Hazardous Substances like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify hazardous substances found in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to identify hazardous substances found in the environment. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify hazardous substances found in the environment.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Handling Hazardous Substances”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify hazardous substances found in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Classify hazardous substances found in the locality

What this means
In this part you learn to classify hazardous substances found in the locality. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify hazardous substances found in the locality.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Handling Hazardous Substances.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify hazardous substances found in the locality. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Handling Hazardous Substances”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Handling Hazardous Substances is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Handling Hazardous Substances”. (skill: identify hazardous substances found in the environment)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Handling Hazardous Substances. (skill: classify hazardous substances found in the locality)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment)

Example 4: State one safety rule before practising “Handling Hazardous Substances”. (skill: appreciate the importance of observing safety when handling hazardous substances)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Handling Hazardous Substances to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify hazardous substances found in the environment.
3. Practise this skill: classify hazardous substances found in the locality.
4. Practise this skill: describe safe ways of handling hazardous substances in the environment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Handling Hazardous Substances from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Handling Hazardous Substances: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Handling Hazardous Substances?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are hazardous substances labelled?
2. How are hazardous substances handled?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Handling Hazardous Substances means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify hazardous substances found in the environment.
5. Be able to: classify hazardous substances found in the locality.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
